newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-CBA still sees flat 96/97 profit.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-CBA still sees flat 96/97 profit.

text.p: Commonwealth Bank of Australia (CBA) chief executive David Murray said on Sunday the bank still expected a flat result for the 1996/97 year ending June 30.

"I think the oulook is still as we put it at June and that is for a flat year, because we're also incurring the funding cost of that billion dollar buy back of shares," Murray told the Nine Network's Business Sunday programme.

The Commonwealth Bank agreed in April to buy back 100 million shares at no more than A$10.70 a share from the Australian government, as part of the government's plan to sell its remaining 50.4 percent stake in the bank.
"With that and the slight squeeze in margins -- and of course margins are being squeezed elsewhere -- we see flat profit this year but a slight increase in earnings per share," he said.

The dominance of banks in the profitable housing loan market has been challenged recently by the entry of non-bank mortgage managers -- funded by mortgage-back securities to wholesale investors -- who have been offering cheaper interest rates on mortgages.
These lenders accounted for about nine percent of new housing loan approvals in the past year.
Murray said the bank, one of Australia's 'Big Four' banks, had increased its market share of housing finance approvals by about six percentage points since June.
He said the recent rise in the Commonwealth Bank's shares was mainly due to the soft long bond yield.
"There's quite a strong correlation between our share price and the bond yield so it doesn't really surprise me," he said.
Long bond yields have fallen recently on expectations of another cut in official interest rates before the end of calendar 1996.

Commonwealth Bank shares closed at A$11.58 on Friday, compared with around A$11.18 in August, after it announced a 13.8 percent rise 1995/96 net profit to A$1.119 billion, and around A$10.25 in July, ahead of the listing of its instalment receipts, which were issued after the sale of the government's stake.
